  An item with waiting_on: owner continues with work-decide, whatever its stage.

Statuses:
  Backlog      Logged; requirements are still being worked out (stages 01-02).
  Ready        Requirements approved; work can start (stage 03).
  In Progress  The item is active (stages 04-11). It does not mean building has started.
  In Review    The result is in a pull request, being deployed, or being written into the specifications (stages 12-14).
  Done         The owner accepted the result. Set only by toolkit work finish.
  Cancelled    Work stopped without the result. Set only by toolkit work cancel.

Types:
  discovery               Finding out what is needed.
  solution-design         Designing how something gets built.
  build                   Producing a change. Needs approved requirements before stage 03.
  data-load               Loading or changing data. Needs approved requirements before stage 03.
  repository-maintenance  Keeping the repository in order.
  research                Answering a question with sources.
  task                    A small piece of work.
  bug                     Something that does not work as it should.
  enhancement             An improvement to something that works.
  Other lower-case words are allowed as types.

Priorities: urgent, high, medium, low. Waiting on: owner, agent, external: <who>, none. Delivery: agent-led, owner-led, not-offered.

Approval gates:
  Requirements approval: asked by work-requirements; recorded with toolkit work approve <id> --requirements --by <name>. build and data-load items cannot reach stage 03 or later without it. Sets stage 03 when the item is earlier.
  Design approval: asked by solution-design; recorded with toolkit work approve <id> --design --by <name>. The design stays proposed until the owner approves it.
  Result approval (stage 11): asked by work-check; recorded with toolkit work approve <id> --result --by <name>. The owner approves the result before it is finished.
  Done: asked by work-finish; recorded with toolkit work finish <id> --by <name> --evidence <text> [--quote <owner's words>]. Only this command sets Done. With no recorded result approval it needs --quote, the owner's own words approving the result, and records that approval.
  Cancel: asked by work-finish; recorded with toolkit work cancel <id> --reason <text>. Only this command sets Cancelled. The reason is the owner's words.
  Delivery offer and team: asked by work-delegate; recorded with toolkit work set <id> --delivery agent-led|owner-led. Offered once per goal; the detail goes in Notes > Decisions and context.
  Project-wide decision: asked by work-decide; recorded with toolkit decision add --decision <text> --why <text> --by <name>. A row in DECISIONS.md at the project root.

What counts as approval:
  - Only the owner's explicit words count as approval. Quote them in the record.
  - A question, a suggestion, a tentative answer, or a saved draft is not approval.
  - Approval never covers merge, deployment, spending, or publishing.
  - Approval survives later stages. A stage alone does not prove approval: check the approval field.
  - A hand change that skips a gate is kept and reported as a question for the owner. It is never reverted.

Rules:
  - Status follows stage: 01-02 Backlog, 03 Ready, 04-11 In Progress, 12-14 In Review.
  - Stages may be skipped, repeated, and revisited. Record a one-line reason when a move is not obvious.
  - Pull-request stages (12) apply only to repository work.
  - Blocking is waiting_on plus the Overview Blockers line, never a status.
  - An item waiting on the owner continues with work-decide, whatever its stage.
  - An item that breaks an approval gate continues with work-decide until the owner answers.
  - An item at 11 User approval whose result approval is recorded continues with work-finish.
  - A Done or Cancelled item continues with nothing: it is finished. Reopen it with toolkit work set <id> --stage <s> --reopen.
